site.name: Nexoma Books
site.description: Technical books published by Nexoma Labs LLC — practitioner titles on AI engineering, prompt engineering, and production AI systems.

series.title: Applied AI Engineering
series.short_description: A four-volume practitioner series that treats AI work as an engineering discipline — from how the machinery works to running it in production.
description: Most AI books teach either the theory of how models work or a catalogue of prompting tricks. Neither prepares you to ship and operate a system that other people depend on.

Applied AI Engineering treats AI work as an engineering discipline. A reader who finishes the series can take an ambiguous business requirement and produce a system that is designed, implemented, evaluated, secured, deployed, monitored, and maintainable — and can explain and defend every decision along the way.

The series is deliberately written to outlive individual model releases. Techniques are taught as engineering principles, with vendor-specific implementations shown as worked examples rather than as the subject matter.
series.author: Dr. Ahmed AlSalih

audience.primary: Software engineers, AI/ML engineers, technical architects, and senior developers moving into AI system work.
audience.secondary: Computer science students (upper undergraduate and graduate), technical product managers, solution architects, and educators teaching applied AI.
audience.not: Readers looking for a prompt cookbook, and researchers looking for novel results.

progression.line: How the machinery works and what it costs

Run it in production without it hurting anyone

methodology.name: The Review Loop
methodology.summary: The series has one recurring methodology that distinguishes it from comparable books: a disciplined create / execute / evaluate / critique / improve / re-test loop, taught explicitly and applied in every volume.
methodology.rule: The model that produces an artifact is never the model that evaluates it. Reviewers are queried independently rather than asked to role-play a committee in a single response, and disagreement between reviewers is preserved and reported, not synthesized away.

boards.name: Review Board
boards.question: Is this correct, secure, maintainable, and usable?

boards.name: Critique Board
boards.question: Is this worth building, and what is the strongest case against it?

volumes.title: Foundations
volumes.subtitle: How Modern AI Systems Actually Work
volumes.status_note: Manuscript complete and validated. Release pending final production checks.
volumes.mission: Understand how modern AI systems actually work, what they cost, where they fail, and why engineering discipline is required to use them well.
volumes.prerequisites: Basic computer literacy. Programming experience is helpful but not required — every laboratory provides a complete starting point.
blurb: Volume I builds the conceptual and economic foundation the rest of the series stands on. It moves from what artificial intelligence is, through machine learning, neural networks, and deep learning, into the transformer architecture and the large language models built on it.
It ends where practical work begins: a full chapter on prompt engineering foundations that explains why prompting works in terms of the underlying mechanism, not as a list of tricks.
outcomes: Explain the evolution from symbolic AI to foundation models.
Distinguish AI, machine learning, deep learning, and generative AI precisely.
Explain the transformer architecture and why it displaced recurrent models.
Describe how an LLM turns text into tokens, and tokens into a next-token distribution.
Explain how reasoning models differ from standard LLMs, and when the extra cost is justified.
Identify the characteristic failure modes of LLMs and explain their mechanical causes.
Explain why prompt engineering works, in terms of the underlying mechanism.
chapters: History and Evolution of Artificial Intelligence

volumes.title: Prompt Engineering
volumes.subtitle: Designing, Testing, and Defending AI Instructions
volumes.status_note: Chapter plan approved. Drafting in progress.
volumes.mission: Make a model do what you specify, provably — through systematic prompt design, structured outputs, evaluation, and the Review Board methodology.
volumes.prerequisites: Volume I, or equivalent working knowledge of LLMs. Programming experience in at least one language.
blurb: Volume II is about control. It treats a prompt as an engineered artifact with a specification, a test suite, and a regression history — not as a phrase you tune until the output looks right.
It introduces the series' signature methodology: the AI Review Board and the Critique Board, two distinct evaluation structures that answer different questions about a system you are about to ship.
chapters: System Prompts and Persistent Instruction Files
Prompt Caching as a Design Constraint

volumes.title: Context and Agents
volumes.subtitle: Retrieval, Tools, and Autonomous Systems
volumes.status_note: Chapter plan approved. Drafting begins after Volume II.
volumes.mission: Give a model context, tools, memory, and autonomy — safely.
volumes.prerequisites: Volumes I and II, or equivalent. Comfortable building and testing software.
blurb: Volume III covers the layer where most real systems are actually built: context pipelines, retrieval, tool use, and the agent control surface.
Agents are treated as an engineering problem of control and containment rather than one of capability. Hooks, skills, subagents, tool permissions, and sandboxed execution get first-class treatment.
chapters: Advanced Retrieval: Hybrid Search and Reranking
Hooks: Deterministic Control of the Agent Lifecycle

volumes.title: Production Systems
volumes.subtitle: Deploying, Securing, and Operating AI at Scale
volumes.status_note: Chapter plan approved. Drafting begins after Volume III.
volumes.mission: Run an AI system in production without it hurting anyone.
volumes.prerequisites: Volumes I to III, or equivalent production engineering experience.
blurb: Volume IV is the operations volume: deployment, inference optimization, security, observability, governance, cost, and the full lifecycle of a model in production.
Prompt injection, red-teaming, human-in-the-loop approval gates, model migration, and regulatory compliance are treated as core engineering concerns rather than appendices.
chapters: Regression Testing and CI for AI Systems
